blocks.text: Maple Ridge Homes for Sale: streets and boundaries

items.t: Maple Ridge is one city with two halves: an urban southwest around Haney and the Town Centre, and a rural east and north in Whonnock, Thornhill and the farm belt.
The Fraser River forms the south boundary, Pitt Meadows is the west boundary, Mission is the east boundary, and Golden Ears Provincial Park closes the north.

The board divides the city into 12 sub-areas, including Albion, Cottonwood, East Central, North, Northeast, Northwest, Silver Valley, Southwest, Thornhill, Websters Corners, West Central and Whonnock.
Haney is the historic name for the downtown core; the City's current name for the same area is Town Centre, around Haney Place and Dewdney Trunk Road.

blocks.text: Maple Ridge Homes for Sale: the housing stock

items.t: City housing splits by geography: urban detached, townhouse and condominium product in the southwest and Albion, and acreage houses on rural and farm zones in the east and north.
The standard urban house zone is RS-1 in Zoning Bylaw No. 7600-2019, with subdivision minimums of 668.0 square metres, 18.0 metres width and 27.0 metres depth.
Rural zone minimums in the same bylaw reach 2.0 hectares in A-1, 4.0 hectares in A-2 and 8.0 hectares in A-3, which is why east-side lots cannot be compared with Town Centre lots.

blocks.text: Maple Ridge Homes for Sale: rules that affect buyers

items.t: Council adopted Official Community Plan (OCP) updates on November 25, 2025, and updated area plans for Town Centre, Hammond, Silver Valley and Albion in the same 2025 cycle.

blocks.text: Maple Ridge Homes for Sale: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: The city has two West Coast Express stations, Port Haney at 22300 River Road and Maple Meadows at 20010 Dunn Avenue, not one.
A "North" address and a "Northwest" address are different board sub-areas in Maple Ridge, so a listing search under one name misses the other.
Golden Ears Way is the City-named approach route to the Golden Ears Bridge, and its expansion is a TransLink-owned project the City advocates for in Maple Ridge Moves.

blocks.text: Maple Ridge Homes for Sale: development and new projects

items.t: Abernethy Way Corridor Improvements, 210 Street to 256 Street — City transportation project, current: four-lane widening east to 240 Street with a future 256 Street connection; the 232 to 240 Street phase has design and acquisition in 2025–2026 and construction beginning in 2027 (status read November 3, 2026).

240 Street Bridge north of 124 Avenue — City capital item, pre-planning: a second Alouette River crossing aligned with 240 Street, with a $55 million initial Class B estimate in the 2026–2030 capital plan, supporting access to Silver Valley.
North 256 Street Industrial Lands Area Plan — City plan, in development: about 600 acres of industrial land whose opening depends on the Abernethy Way extension to 256 Street.

blocks.text: Maple Ridge Homes for Sale: costs and taxes

items.t: Maple Ridge's 2026 general residential property-tax rate is $2.8643 per $1,000 of taxable value, under Property Tax Rates Bylaw No. 8099-2026, adopted May 12, 2026.
The full 2026 residential mill rate in the City's rate summary is $4.53578 per $1,000 including school, BC Assessment, Metro Vancouver and TransLink levies.
Council set the 2026 property-tax increase at 3.5%, about $101 for a property assessed at the city average of $1.04 million.

blocks.text: Maple Ridge Homes for Sale: getting around

items.t: West Coast Express runs weekday trains between Waterfront and Mission City through Port Haney and Maple Meadows stations.
The R3 Lougheed Hwy RapidBus runs Haney Place to Coquitlam Central Station, and route 701 runs Coquitlam Central via Haney Place, Maple Meadows and Pitt Meadows stations.
Lougheed Highway (Highway 7) is the east-west highway, Dewdney Trunk Road is the parallel Town Centre arterial, and Golden Ears Way leads to the Golden Ears Bridge to Langley and Surrey.

blocks.text: Maple Ridge Homes for Sale: risks and due diligence

items.t: Check ALR status parcel by parcel in the east and north farm belt on the Agricultural Land Commission map; city zoning alone does not settle farm use.
Check creek and steep-slope ground in Silver Valley, Thornhill and the Kanaka Creek corridor against the OCP development-permit areas for the exact lot.
